Two integrations by parts give the signed cell trapezoid difference with the quadratic weight and the distributional derivative of g′. Its maximum is a²/8. The endpoint values of the weight are zero, so jumps exactly at mesh points contribute zero. A cutoff inside a cell contributes its derivative atom. Summed trapezoids have half weight at zero, giving the stated sample correction and a/8 times the total variation.

On each active interval, the product rule gives the two derivative bounds using |s| ≤ 1, B ≤ 2d+1, affine bracket at most 1 and base at most 2. For d = 2 the second-power derivative term is identically absent, including the left corner with zero base. Integrating the second bound over length at most one and adding the sole endpoint jump yields [(d−1)(9d+2)+2(5d+1)]2^(d−3) = V_d. The monotone mass derivative has variation d. This gives the combined quadrature remainder a(V_d/4+d/8).

Rescaling the moving endpoint x = uy yields the polynomial-in-a right integral with coefficients continuous in v. In the moving-domain derivative, the first endpoint term is zero. The second is the product (−dv Z(u)^(d−1))(−dv/B), positive with the stated coefficient. The sum of the bounds on the two interior terms and the endpoint term has numerator (d−1)(d−2)+4d(d−1)+4d² = 9d²−7d+2. The d = 2 zero coefficient and the v = 0 constant integral cause no singularity. Taylor's bound after division by a is T_d a/2.

Direct differentiation at a = 0 gives the bracket 1+[(d−1)(d+1+dv)+dv]x = 1+(d²−1+d²v)x. Its bound at x ≤ 1/(d+1) is d(2d+1)/(d+1), proving K_d. The right sample at zero has a-derivative −v(1+av)^(d−2)(1+d²av). The half-endpoint correction changes by at most (d+2)2^(d−4)a = B_da. Combining with the mass and left endpoint values gives the constant −J_d(v)−1/2 and the stated C_d.

The common unshifted kernels are continuous jointly on the fixed compact x-domain. For z ≠ 0 the transformed bracket is (A_z−B_z y)/z and dx = dy/z. Evaluating with oriented limits gives A_z^(d+1)/(d(d+1)B_z^d) = f(z)/d at the upper limit. The affine parts sum to −2/d at opposite tilts. This includes z = −1 where the transformed interval ends at zero. At v = 0 the two equal triangle integrals are each 1/[2(d+1)], so G_d(0) = 0 directly.
